topic.subject: social
topic.title: Consumer rights
topic.scope: consumer exploitation, right to safety, information, choice, redressal, consumer courts, ISI and Agmark

misconceptions.statement: Only poor or uneducated people get cheated by shopkeepers.
misconceptions.why: Students often associate exploitation with lack of literacy rather than systemic market practices.
misconceptions.fix: Exploitation occurs due to information asymmetry and market power, which can affect any consumer regardless of their education level.

probe.question: Can a highly educated professional be exploited in a market transaction?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because they are smart enough to know the real price and quality of goods.

misconceptions.statement: If a product is expensive, it is guaranteed to be of high quality.
misconceptions.why: Students often use price as a heuristic for quality in their daily shopping experiences.
misconceptions.fix: Price does not always reflect quality; sellers may overcharge for inferior or adulterated goods.

probe.question: Is a high-priced item always safe and genuine?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because sellers would not charge a high price for a bad product.

misconceptions.statement: Having a right means the government will automatically fix any problem I have with a product.
misconceptions.why: Students often confuse the existence of a legal right with the automatic enforcement of that right.
misconceptions.fix: Rights provide a legal framework, but the consumer must actively seek redressal through complaints and evidence.

probe.question: If you buy a defective phone, what happens next?
probe.wrong_answer: The government will automatically notice the defect and force the shopkeeper to replace it.

misconceptions.statement: ISI and Agmark are the same thing and can be used on any product.
misconceptions.why: Students often see these as generic 'quality stamps' without understanding their specific sector-based application.
misconceptions.fix: ISI is for industrial products, while Agmark is specifically for agricultural and food products.

probe.question: Which mark should you look for on a packet of honey?
probe.wrong_answer: The ISI mark, because it is a standard quality mark for all goods.

misconceptions.statement: Consumer courts are only for very large cases involving millions of rupees.
misconceptions.why: Media coverage often highlights high-profile corporate litigation, leading students to believe small disputes are ignored.
misconceptions.fix: Consumer courts are designed to handle disputes of all sizes, including small-value items, through a simplified process.

probe.question: Can you go to a consumer court for a faulty electric bulb?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the court is too busy and only deals with big company frauds.
